sections.content: How many people are "bus and coach drivers"?

121,005 people

were counted on the census as "bus and coach drivers" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Bus and coach drivers drive road passenger-carrying vehicles such as buses, coaches and mini-buses.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "bus and coach drivers" there were more men than women (90.4% compared with 9.6%).

This means "bus and coach drivers" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "transport and mobile machine drivers and operatives".

Men made up 90.4% and women made up 9.6% of "bus and coach drivers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "bus and coach drivers" included:

  • butchers
  • aircraft pilots and air traffic controllers
  • metal making and treating process operatives

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "bus and coach drivers" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "bus and coach drivers", 16.4% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "bus and coach drivers" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "bus and coach drivers" included:

  • garage managers and proprietors
  • podiatrists
  • counsellors

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "bus and coach drivers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "bus and coach drivers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "bus and coach drivers", 9.9% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (75.9% compared with 24.1%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (86.2%) than self-employed (13.8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
